There is no skirt (der Rock) or belt (der Gürtel) in the picture.

questions.stem: Type the adjective with its ending: "Zur Party trägt sie ein ___ Kleid." (rot)
questions.explanation: das Kleid is neuter, and "ein" doesn't show that, so the adjective takes the -es of "das": ein rotes Kleid. It's the same in the nominative and the accusative (here it's the object of trägt).

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the ending the adjective needs.
left: Ich gehe mit einem warm___ Schal.
questions.explanation: After ein-words: masculine nominative -er (ein warmer Mantel), masculine accusative -en (einen warmen Mantel), feminine -e (eine warme Jacke), neuter nominative and accusative -es (ein warmes Hemd), and every dative -en (mit einem warmen Schal). -em never follows an ein-word: einem already shows the dative.

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "mein alter Mantel" (masculine nominative, -er), "eine gestreifte Bluse" (feminine, -e) and "ein kariertes Hemd" (neuter, -es) are right. After a dative article the ending is always -en: mit einem roten Schal. And in the plural after keine the ending is -en: keine bequemen Schuhe.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to ask: "Can I try on the blue jacket?"
questions.explanation: Kann ich die blaue Jacke anprobieren? In a yes/no question the modal verb comes first, then the subject, and the infinitive goes to the end. With a modal, anprobieren stays in one piece at the end.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the department store.

image.alt: A department store in cross-section with three floors and four numbered things: a lift on the left, an escalator, a changing room with a curtain, and a till counter.

questions.explanation: 1 der Aufzug (the lift, which goes to every floor), 2 die Rolltreppe (the escalator), 3 die Umkleidekabine (the changing room, with a curtain), 4 die Kasse (the till, where you pay and get your Kassenzettel). A Tüte is a bag, and der Ausgang is the exit.

questions.stem: Type the adjective with its ending: "Welchen Pullover nehmen Sie?" – "Den ___, bitte." (blau)
questions.explanation: The noun (Pullover) is left out, but the ending stays: den blauen (masculine accusative after "den", so -en). "Den blau" without an ending is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Match each verb to the situation.
choices: You swap the shirt for a bigger size.
You bring the shoes back and get your money.
You complain that the toaster is broken.
You put the coat on in the changing room.
questions.explanation: umtauschen = to exchange for something else; zurückgeben = to give back (for a refund); reklamieren = to complain about a faulty product; anprobieren = to try on. Paying at the till would be bezahlen.

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: After der-words the adjective ends in -e in the five special boxes (der neue Rock, das schwarze Kleid) and -en everywhere else (mit dem neuen Aufzug). In the plural after die it's -en: die neuen Schuhe. And dieser shows masculine nominative itself, so the adjective needs only -e: dieser blaue Pullover.

questions.stem: Type the ordinal number with its ending: "Die Damenabteilung ist im ___ Stock." (zweit-)
questions.explanation: im = in dem, a dative der-word, so the ordinal takes -en: im zweiten Stock. Ordinal numbers take adjective endings like any other adjective.

questions.stem: Name the numbered kitchen things.

image.alt: Six numbered kitchen things on a worktop: a saucepan with a lid, a frying pan, a plate, and a fork, a knife and a spoon standing upright.

questions.explanation: 1 der Topf (saucepan), 2 die Pfanne (frying pan), 3 der Teller (plate), 4 die Gabel (fork), 5 das Messer (knife), 6 der Löffel (spoon). There is no cup (die Tasse) or glass (das Glas) in the picture.

questions.stem: Type the adjective with its ending: "Sie trinkt Kaffee mit ___ Milch." (warm)
questions.explanation: mit takes the dative, die Milch is feminine, and there's no article, so the adjective takes the ending of the dative article "der": mit warmer Milch.

questions.stem: Which table does each adjective follow?
questions.explanation: With no article the adjective shows the case itself (frischer Fisch). After der and alle (der-words) it takes -e or -en (der frische Fisch, alle frischen Eier). After ein it takes -er here (ein frischer Fisch). A number like zwei doesn't count as an article, so zwei frische Eier follows the no-article table.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Brot mit frischem Käse ist lecker.
Sie trinkt Tee mit warm Milch.
questions.explanation: kaltes Wasser (neuter accusative, -es), mit frischem Käse (masculine dative, -em) and braunen Zucker (masculine accusative, -en) are right. Plural with no article in the nominative takes -e: Frische Eier sind teuer. And with no article the adjective must show the case: mit warmer Milch.

questions.stem: Put the steps of Grandma's pancake recipe from the lesson in order.
choices: Mehl, Salz und Zucker in eine Schüssel geben
Die Eier und die Milch dazugeben und mischen
Den Teig zehn Minuten stehen lassen
Öl in der Pfanne heiß machen
Die Pfannkuchen auf beiden Seiten braten
questions.explanation: The recipe starts with the dry ingredients in a bowl, adds the eggs and milk, then the batter rests for ten minutes. Only then is the oil heated, the pancakes are fried on both sides, and they're served with fresh fruit (or sugar and cinnamon).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the landscape.

image.alt: A landscape with six numbered parts: trees on a hill, the hill itself, a meadow with flowers, a river, a striped field, and a farmhouse with a barn. A snowy mountain stands in the background.

questions.explanation: 1 der Wald (the trees, a forest), 2 der Hügel (hill), 3 die Wiese (meadow, with flowers), 4 der Fluss (river), 5 das Feld (a ploughed field), 6 der Bauernhof (farm). There's no coast (die Küste) and no village (das Dorf), only one farm.

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Berlin hat ___ Einwohner als Hamburg." (viel)
questions.explanation: viel is irregular: viel, mehr, am meisten. mehr never takes an ending: mehr Einwohner. "vieler" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Match each adjective to its comparative.
questions.explanation: gut – besser and viel – mehr are irregular. hoch loses its c and adds an umlaut: höher. nah and alt just add an umlaut: näher, älter. "guter" is gut with an adjective ending, not a comparative.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Das Dorf ist ruhiger als die Stadt.
Mein Bruder ist so groß wie ich.
Die Stadt ist lauter wie das Dorf.
Hier ist der Fluss am breitesten.
questions.explanation: After a comparative use als (ruhiger als), for equality so … wie (so groß wie), and after a verb the superlative is am …-sten, with an extra e after t (am breitesten). "lauter wie" should be "lauter als", and before a noun the comparative needs an ending, with hoch becoming höher-: der höhere Berg.

questions.stem: Type the superlative with its ending: "Die Zugspitze ist der ___ Berg in Deutschland." (hoch)
questions.explanation: hoch is irregular: hoch, höher, am höchsten. Before a noun after "der" (masculine nominative) the superlative takes -e: der höchste Berg.

questions.stem: Grammar books call the endings of adjectives with no article (frischer Fisch, kaltes Wasser) the …
questions.explanation: With no article the adjective does all the work itself with the endings of der, das, dem: that's the strong declension. Weak endings (-e/-en) come after der-words, and mixed ones after ein-words. Strong verbs are a different idea (fahren, fuhr, gefahren).

questions.stem: Which declension does each adjective follow?
questions.explanation: After der-words (der, alle) the declension is weak; after ein-words (ein, meinen) it's mixed; with no article (neuer Wein) it's strong. The ending alone doesn't tell you: neuer is mixed in "ein neuer Rock" and strong in "neuer Wein". Look at the word in front.

questions.stem: What does "Vorsicht, kochendes Wasser!" warn you about?
choices: water that has been boiled and cooled
water that is boiling right now
water that must not be boiled
questions.explanation: kochend is the present participle of kochen: the water is boiling at this moment. Water that has been boiled is gekochtes Wasser (past participle), and it may be cold by now.

questions.stem: Type the present participle with its ending: "Ich höre die ___ Kinder im Garten." (lachen)
questions.explanation: The present participle is the infinitive + d: lachend. Before a noun it takes the normal ending; after die in the plural that's -en: die lachenden Kinder (the laughing children).

questions.stem: How do you say "The soup is boiling"?
questions.explanation: German has no "is …-ing" form: use the plain present tense, Die Suppe kocht. The present participle (kochend) mostly stands before a noun: die kochende Suppe. "Die Suppe ist gekocht" means it has been cooked.

questions.stem: A café menu: "Frisch ___ Orangensaft" (gepresst). Which form is right?
questions.explanation: der Saft is masculine, the menu item is nominative and there's no article, so the participle takes the strong ending -er: frisch gepresster Orangensaft. frisch is an adverb describing gepresst, so it has no ending.

questions.stem: Type the adjective made from "die Schweiz": "Ich esse gern Brot mit ___ Käse." (Swiss)
questions.explanation: The place-name adjective is Schweizer: capital letter, and no ending in any case: mit Schweizer Käse. "Schweizerem" is a common mistake. (The normal adjective schweizerisch would take an ending: mit schweizerischem Käse.)

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Place-name adjectives in -er never change: der Kölner Dom, in der Berliner U-Bahn, mit Wiener Schnitzel, die Frankfurter Würstchen. schweizerisch is an ordinary adjective, so it takes the normal ending: ein schweizerischer Käse.

questions.stem: John F. Kennedy said "Ich bin ein Berliner" in 1963. What is true?
choices: It meant "I am a doughnut", and Berliners laughed at him.
It was correct German, and his audience understood what he meant.
He should have said "Ich bin ein Berlin".
In Berlin, a Berliner is the usual word for a doughnut.
questions.explanation: The doughnut story is a popular myth: the sentence is correct German for "I am a Berliner" (here in a figurative sense), and the crowd understood it that way. In Berlin itself a doughnut is usually called a Pfannkuchen, not a Berliner.

questions.stem: At the museum desk: "Zwei ___ und ein Kind, bitte."
questions.explanation: Erwachsene is an adjectival noun. After a number there's no article, so it takes the strong plural ending -e: zwei Erwachsene. "Erwachsenen" is right after die or in the dative (mit zwei Erwachsenen).

questions.stem: Type the noun with its ending: "Mein Nachbar kommt aus Hamburg. Er ist ein ___." (German, a man)
questions.explanation: der Deutsche is an adjectival noun, so after ein (masculine nominative) it takes the mixed ending -er: ein Deutscher. A German woman is eine Deutsche.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
questions.explanation: After a number an adjectival noun takes the strong ending -e in the nominative: zwei Erwachsene (like zwei Deutsche). Meine Verwandten is right: after a possessive in the plural, -en. Österreicher is an ordinary noun, so zwei Österreicher has no ending.

questions.stem: Read the sign. What is free?

image.alt: A market stall sign for Marktstand Huber listing orange juice, potato soup, stuffed peppers, sausages and Swiss cheese with prices, then coffee for adults, cocoa for children, and the Saturday opening hours.

questions.explanation: "Kakao für Kinder gratis": cocoa is free for children. Coffee for adults (Kaffee für Erwachsene) costs 2,00 €, and the orange juice and cheese have prices too.

questions.stem: On the same sign: "Gefüllte Paprika mit Reis". Why does gefüllt end in -e?

image.alt: A market stall sign for Marktstand Huber listing orange juice, potato soup, stuffed peppers, sausages and Swiss cheese with prices, then coffee for adults, cocoa for children, and the Saturday opening hours.

choices: There is no article, and Paprika is feminine (or plural) and nominative.
questions.explanation: die Paprika is feminine (Duden also allows der Paprika; one masculine Paprika would be "Gefüllter Paprika"). The menu item stands alone (nominative) with no article, so the participle takes the strong ending of "die": -e. If the sign means several peppers (plural), the strong ending is -e as well. Participles don't have a fixed ending; they take whatever ending an adjective would take there.

questions.stem: How do you say "Switzerland is much smaller than Germany"?
choices: Die Schweiz ist sehr kleiner als Deutschland.
Die Schweiz ist viel kleiner als Deutschland.
Die Schweiz ist viel kleiner wie Deutschland.
Die Schweiz ist mehr klein als Deutschland.
questions.explanation: With a comparative, "much" is viel: viel kleiner als. sehr only goes with the plain adjective (sehr klein), the comparative is followed by als, not wie, and German never uses mehr + adjective for a comparative.

questions.stem: Austria is about 83,900 km², Switzerland about 41,300 km². Complete: "Österreich ist ungefähr ___ so groß wie die Schweiz."
questions.explanation: 83,900 ÷ 41,300 ≈ 2, so Austria is about twice as big: doppelt (or zweimal) so groß wie die Schweiz.

questions.stem: "Der Großglockner ist hoch, aber die Dufourspitze ist noch höher." What does "noch höher" mean?
questions.explanation: noch + comparative means "even …" or "… still": noch höher = even higher. It suggests that the first mountain is already high.

questions.stem: Match the German to the English.
questions.explanation: doppelt so … wie = twice as … as; halb so … wie = half as … as; zweit- + superlative = second-…; mit Abstand = by far; mindestens = at least. "At most" would be höchstens.

questions.stem: Type the superlative with its ending: "Der Bodensee ist einer der ___ Seen in Mitteleuropa." (groß)
questions.explanation: In "one of the …" the noun is plural and the superlative after der ends in -en: einer der größten Seen. einer is masculine because der See is masculine.

questions.stem: How do you say "one of the highest mountains"?
questions.explanation: der Berg is masculine, so "one" is einer; the noun is plural (Berge) and the superlative ends in -en: einer der höchsten Berge. "eine" would be for a feminine noun (eine der größten Städte), and "höheren" is the comparative.

questions.stem: Put the mountains in order from the lowest to the highest.
questions.explanation: Zugspitze (Germany) 2,962 m, Großglockner (Austria) 3,798 m, Dufourspitze (Switzerland) 4,634 m. Germany is the biggest of the three countries, but it has the lowest highest mountain.

questions.stem: Which statements are true, according to the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: Deutschland hat ungefähr neunmal so viele Einwohner wie Österreich.
Die Schweiz ist größer als Österreich.
Österreich hat etwas mehr Einwohner als die Schweiz.
Die Zugspitze ist höher als der Großglockner.
Berlin ist mit Abstand die größte Stadt Deutschlands.
questions.explanation: Germany has about 83 million people against Austria's 9.2 million (about nine times as many); Austria (9.2 million) has slightly more than Switzerland (9.1 million); and Berlin is by far Germany's biggest city. But Switzerland is only about half the size of Austria, and the Zugspitze (2,962 m) is lower than the Großglockner (3,798 m).

questions.stem: What is special about Bern?
choices: It is the biggest city in Switzerland.
It is officially called the "Bundesstadt": Switzerland has no official capital.
It is the capital of Austria.
questions.explanation: Bern is the seat of the Swiss government and parliament, but officially it's the Bundesstadt (federal city); Switzerland has no official capital. The biggest Swiss city is Zürich, Austria's capital is Wien, and Bern isn't on Lake Constance.

questions.stem: Lake Constance (der Bodensee) is shared by three countries. Which is the largest lake lying entirely inside Germany?
questions.explanation: The Müritz in Mecklenburg is the largest lake entirely inside Germany. The Bodensee is far bigger but shared with Austria and Switzerland, the Genfer See (Lake Geneva) lies in Switzerland and France, and the Nordsee is a sea.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ Schweizer sprechen Deutsch." (Most Swiss people speak German.)
questions.explanation: Before a noun, "most" is die meisten: die meisten Schweizer. am meisten goes after a verb (Wer hat am meisten gegessen?), and meistens means "usually, mostly".

questions.stem: The Großglockner is 3,798 m high and the Zugspitze 2,962 m. Complete: "Der Großglockner ist um ___ Meter höher als die Zugspitze." Give only the number.
questions.explanation: 3,798 − 2,962 = 836, so: um 836 Meter höher. um + amount gives the exact difference.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
choices: Wien ist die zweitgrößte Stadt im deutschsprachigen Raum.
Wir fahren so früh wie möglich los.
Der Rhein ist sehr länger als der Main.
Die Fahrt dauert mindestens drei Stunden.
questions.explanation: sehr can't go with a comparative: it must be viel länger. The other sentences are correct: zweitgrößte is one word, so … wie möglich means "as … as possible", and mindestens means "at least".

questions.stem: Complete: "Hamburg hat nicht so ___ Einwohner wie Berlin."
questions.explanation: Einwohner are things you count, so use viele: nicht so viele Einwohner wie Berlin. viel is for amounts you don't count (so viel Zeit), and mehr belongs with als (mehr Einwohner als).

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in Lena's living room.

image.alt: A living room on moving day with six numbered things: something hanging from the ceiling, something on the wall above the sofa, something at the window, something on the sofa, something on the floor in front of the sofa, and a box marked Küche on the floor.

questions.explanation: 1 die Lampe hangs from the ceiling (an der Decke), 2 das Bild hangs on the wall above the sofa, 3 der Vorhang hangs at the window, 4 das Kissen lies on the sofa, 5 der Teppich lies on the floor in front of the sofa, 6 der Karton stands on the floor. The cooker (der Herd) and the dishwasher (die Spülmaschine) belong in the kitchen, not in this picture.

questions.stem: Type the past participles: "Gestern hat der Teppich im Flur ___. Jetzt habe ich ihn ins Schlafzimmer ___."
questions.explanation: The first sentence says where the rug was (Wo? im Flur, no object), so it's the being verb liegen: hat gelegen. In the second, I put it somewhere (Wohin? ins Schlafzimmer, object ihn), so it's the putting verb legen: habe gelegt.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its perfect form.
questions.explanation: The putting verbs are regular: gelegt, gesetzt (and gehängt for hanging something up). The being verbs are irregular: gelegen, gesessen, gehangen. "Gesitzt" and "geliegt" don't exist.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the accusative correctly, because something moves to a new place? Select all that apply.
choices: Wir stellen den Karton in den Keller.
Die Kinder spielen in den Garten.
Sie hängt die Jacke an die Tür.
Die Katze liegt auf das Sofa.
questions.explanation: "den Karton in den Keller stellen" and "die Jacke an die Tür hängen" are both movement to a new place (Wohin?), so the accusative is right. Playing in the garden happens in one place (Wo?): im Garten. Lying is a position: Die Katze liegt auf dem Sofa.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to ask: "Where did you put the key?"
questions.explanation: Question word first (Wohin), then the auxiliary hast in position 2, the subject du, the object den Schlüssel, and the past participle gelegt at the end: Wohin hast du den Schlüssel gelegt?

questions.stem: Match each time phrase to its meaning.
choices: for a planned period of two years
questions.explanation: vor + dative looks back from now (ago); seit + dative started in the past and is still going on; in + dative looks forward from now; für + accusative is a planned length of time. "Until" would be bis.

questions.stem: Complete: "We're flying to Portugal in three weeks." = "Wir fliegen ___ drei ___ nach Portugal."
questions.explanation: "In" + dative counts forward from now: in drei Wochen. Woche has the plural Wochen, which already ends in -n, so the dative plural doesn't change. "Nach drei Wochen" would mean "after three weeks" (after some other event).

questions.stem: Look at the picture. Which words show movement away from the speaker? Select all that apply.

image.alt: A speaker in the middle labeled ich. An arrow labeled her points towards the speaker from a person on the left; an arrow labeled hin points away from the speaker to a lake on the right.

questions.explanation: hin means away from the speaker, her towards the speaker. The combined words keep that meaning: hinauf (up, away from me) and herunter (down, towards me). So hin and hinauf point away.

questions.stem: Put the times in order, from furthest in the past to furthest in the future.
questions.explanation: vor looks back from now: a year ago is further back than a week ago. in looks forward: three days from now comes before a month from now. jetzt sits in between.

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Bringen Sie das Gepäck bitte ___ oben?" (Would you take the luggage upstairs, please?)
questions.explanation: oben is a place (Wo?): Das Zimmer ist oben. For a direction (Wohin?), put nach in front: nach oben, nach unten, nach draußen.

questions.stem: Match each simple past form to its Konjunktiv II ("would") form.
questions.explanation: Past form + umlaut gives the "would" form: hatte → hätte, konnte → könnte, wurde → würde, musste → müsste. war takes an umlaut and an -e: wäre. "Wöre" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Make the request more polite with one word: "Können Sie mir helfen?" → "___ Sie mir bitte helfen?"
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv II of können is könnten (for Sie): Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen? Without the umlaut, "Konnten Sie mir helfen?" means "Were you able to help me?"

questions.stem: Put the parts in order: "If I had time, I would come along."
questions.explanation: In the wenn clause the verb (hätte) goes to the end. Then comes the comma, and the main clause starts with its verb (würde) because the whole wenn clause is in position 1: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich mitkommen.

questions.stem: Which are Konjunktiv II ("would") forms rather than simple past forms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: hätte, wäre and dürfte have the umlaut of the Konjunktiv II. konnte and wurde have no umlaut: they are the simple past (could, was able to; became). Their "would" forms are könnte and würde.

questions.stem: Name the numbered weather symbols.

image.alt: Six numbered weather symbols in tiles: a sun; two clouds; a dark cloud with a lightning bolt; horizontal grey lines; curling wind lines; a cloud with snowflakes.

questions.explanation: 1 the sun: sonnig. 2 clouds: bewölkt. 3 a cloud with lightning: das Gewitter (thunderstorm). 4 grey lines: neblig (foggy, from der Nebel). 5 wind lines: windig. 6 a cloud with snowflakes: der Schnee. No picture shows rain drops (der Regen), and trocken (dry) has no symbol here.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to finish the idea: "Es regnet. ..." (I'm going for a walk anyway.) Start with the linking adverb.
questions.explanation: trotzdem is a linking adverb. In position 1 it is followed directly by the verb (gehe) and then the subject (ich): Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.

questions.stem: Match each linking word to the word order that follows it.
questions.explanation: deshalb and trotzdem are linking adverbs: they take position 1, so the verb comes next (Deshalb bleibe ich …). weil and dass send the verb to the end (…, weil es regnet). denn is a coordinating conjunction in position 0, so the clause keeps its normal order (…, denn es regnet).

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Es ist nicht kalt, ___ warm."
questions.explanation: After a negative (nicht kalt) that is corrected by the second part, use sondern: nicht kalt, sondern warm ("not cold but rather warm"). "aber" would mean "however" and doesn't fit after a corrected negative.

questions.stem: Which sentences have correct word order? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil es regnet.
Ich fahre nach München morgen mit dem Zug.
questions.explanation: After deshalb in position 1 the verb comes next: Deshalb bleiben wir. weil sends the verb to the end: weil es regnet. "Trotzdem ich gehe" needs the verb straight after: Trotzdem gehe ich spazieren. And the middle field goes time, manner, place: Ich fahre morgen mit dem Zug nach München.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Verspätung liegt ___ Stau." (The delay is because of the traffic jam.)
questions.explanation: "liegen an" + dative means "to be because of". der Stau is masculine: an dem Stau, contracted to am Stau. "An den" would be the accusative, which liegen an never takes; "im" and "auf dem" don't give a reason.

questions.stem: What does "In der Zeitung steht, dass die Mieten steigen." mean?
choices: The newspaper is next to the rent.
It says in the paper that rents are rising.
The newspaper is getting more expensive.
The paper says that rents are falling.
questions.explanation: "stehen in" + dative is how German says that something is written in a text: In der Zeitung steht … = It says in the paper … "steigen" means to rise. Nothing is physically standing anywhere: this is a figurative use.

questions.stem: Your friend asks: "Du bist so müde. Woran liegt das?" Which answer fits?
choices: Ich glaube, es liegt daran, dass ich zu wenig schlafe.
questions.explanation: "Woran liegt das?" asks for the reason. The answer uses daran + a dass clause: Es liegt daran, dass ich zu wenig schlafe. "Auf dem Bett" and "im Bett" are real places, not reasons, and "an das Wetter" has the wrong case: liegen an takes the dative (am Wetter).

questions.stem: What does "Mathe liegt mir nicht." mean?
questions.explanation: "jemandem liegen" (person in the dative) means that something suits you or that you're good at it. Mathe liegt mir nicht = I'm not good at maths, it isn't my thing.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in standard German as used in Germany? (I was very attached to my old flat.)
choices: Ich habe sehr an meiner alten Wohnung gehängt.
Ich habe sehr an meine alte Wohnung gehangen.
Ich habe sehr an meiner alten Wohnung gehangen.
Ich bin sehr an meiner alten Wohnung gehangen.
questions.explanation: "hängen an" + dative = to be attached to. It's the being verb, so the perfect is hat gehangen (gehängt is for hanging something up). The case is fixed: an meiner alten Wohnung (dative), not an meine alte Wohnung. Standard German in Germany uses haben here; "ist gehangen" is heard in southern Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

questions.stem: Which of these set phrases uses the accusative?
questions.explanation: aufs = auf das, accusative: Wir fahren aufs Land (to the countryside). vor allem, in der Nähe and auf dem Land (in the countryside) are fixed datives.

questions.stem: Which sentence is colloquial, better kept for friends than for a job interview?
choices: Ich interessiere mich für alte Filme.
Ich stehe total auf alte Filme.
questions.explanation: "auf etwas stehen" (+ accusative) means to be really into something. It's informal, and "total" makes it even more so. The other three are neutral.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wir fahren ___ Wochenende weg." (for the whole weekend, Friday to Sunday)
questions.explanation: über with a stretch of time takes the accusative: übers (über das) Wochenende = for the length of the weekend. "Über dem" is the dative, which doesn't fit. ("Am Wochenende" would also be correct, but it means "at the weekend", not "over the weekend".)

questions.stem: Type the position verb German uses here: "Wo ___ du denn? Ich warte seit einer Stunde!" (Where on earth are you?)
questions.explanation: "Wo steckst du?" (from stecken) asks where a person is, often a bit impatiently. The du form is steckst.

questions.stem: Type the position verb German uses here: "Was ___ in dem Brief?" (What does the letter say?)
questions.explanation: German says that things "stand" in a text: Was steht in dem Brief? The subject is "was", so the verb is in the third person singular: steht.

questions.stem: Match each expression to its meaning.
questions.explanation: All five are figurative uses of the position verbs. "To be written in" would be stehen in (In der Zeitung steht …), which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: In which sentences is the preposition used figuratively, with no real place? Select all that apply.
choices: Unter uns: Ich finde ihn nett.
Die Katze liegt unter dem Tisch.
questions.explanation: "liegen an" (be because of) and "unter uns" (between you and me) don't name places: they are fixed expressions. The box in the hall and the cat under the table are real positions, so the Wo? rule decides the dative there.

questions.stem: Choose the expression that fits each numbered picture.

image.alt: Four numbered panels: a newspaper with the headline Mieten steigen; a line of cars bumper to bumper; a grey cloud with lightning and rain; a person with both arms around a small house, a heart beside it.

questions.explanation: 1 a newspaper: In der Zeitung steht … (it says in the paper). 2 cars that can't move: im Stau stehen. 3 bad weather as the reason for something: Das liegt am Wetter. 4 loving a home: an der Wohnung hängen (to be attached to the flat).

questions.stem: Put the parts in order: "It's because I don't sleep enough."
questions.explanation: Main clause first, verb in position 2: Es liegt daran. daran points forward to the dass clause, and in the dass clause the verb goes to the end: Es liegt daran, dass ich zu wenig schlafe.

questions.stem: Complete correctly: "Morgen ___."
questions.explanation: The weather "es" never disappears. When "Morgen" is in position 1, the verb comes second and es follows it: Morgen regnet es. "Morgen es regnet" breaks the verb-second rule, and "wird regnen" needs es too (Morgen wird es regnen).

questions.stem: Complete: "Gestern ___ es gehagelt."
questions.explanation: Weather verbs form the perfect with haben: Es hat gehagelt, es hat geregnet, es hat geschneit.

questions.stem: Someone says: "Morgen soll es schneien." What do they mean?
choices: They are sure it will snow.
They want it to snow tomorrow.
The forecast says it will snow tomorrow.
questions.explanation: sollen used to pass on information means "they say, apparently": Morgen soll es schneien = It's supposed to snow tomorrow (according to the forecast). It doesn't show that the speaker is sure, and it isn't a wish.

questions.stem: The forecast says "30 Grad". What is that in Fahrenheit?
questions.explanation: F = C × 9/5 + 32: 30 × 9/5 = 54, and 54 + 32 = 86 °F. 54 °F forgets to add 32; 62 °F adds 32 without multiplying by 9/5.

questions.stem: A friend in the US writes that it's 68 °F. How many degrees Celsius is that?
questions.explanation: C = (F − 32) × 5/9: 68 − 32 = 36, and 36 × 5/9 = 20 Grad (room temperature). 36 forgets to multiply by 5/9; 38 multiplies 68 by 5/9 without subtracting 32 first.

questions.stem: Which adjective means "rainy"?
questions.explanation: Most weather adjectives take -ig (sonnig, windig, neblig), but der Regen is an exception: regnerisch. "geregnet" is the past participle (es hat geregnet).

questions.stem: What is "der Föhn" in Munich or Innsbruck?
choices: a cold wind from the North Sea
a warm, dry wind coming down from the Alps
a heavy snowstorm in the mountains
questions.explanation: The Föhn is a warm, dry wind that comes down from the Alps; in Munich and Innsbruck, on the north side, it brings sudden warmth and clear views. In everyday German, der Föhn is also a hairdryer.

questions.stem: You're cold. What do you say?
questions.explanation: For feeling cold, German puts the person in the dative: Mir ist kalt (or: Ich friere). "Ich bin kalt" describes you as a cold person, "Ich mache kalt" isn't German, and "mich" is the accusative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es sind minus fünf Grad." = "Es sind fünf Grad unter ___."
questions.explanation: minus fünf Grad and fünf Grad unter null (five degrees below zero) mean the same.

questions.stem: Convert: 10 °C = ___ °F. Give only the number.
Match each weather verb to its noun.
questions.explanation: hageln – der Hagel (hail), donnern – der Donner (thunder), blitzen – der Blitz (lightning), nieseln – der Nieselregen (drizzle), frieren – der Frost (frost). Fog (der Nebel) has no matching verb in the list: you say es ist neblig.

questions.stem: Name the numbered points on the thermometer.

image.alt: A thermometer with a Celsius and a Fahrenheit scale. Four numbered points: 100 °C = 212 °F, 37 °C = 98,6 °F, 20 °C = 68 °F and 0 °C = 32 °F. A fifth point, −10 °C = 14 °F, has no number.

questions.explanation: 1 water boils at 100 °C (212 °F): Wasser kocht. 2 normal body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F): Körpertemperatur; 39 °C would be Fieber. 3 about 20 °C (68 °F) is Zimmertemperatur. 4 water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F): Wasser gefriert.

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly pass on what the weather forecast says? Select all that apply.
choices: Im Wetterbericht haben sie gesagt, dass es morgen schneit.
questions.explanation: "soll" (er/sie/es form of sollen) passes on a report, and so does an indirect statement with dass. "Morgen schneit" is missing the weather es, and "sollt" is the ihr form, not the es form.

questions.stem: Put the temperatures in order from coldest to warmest.
questions.explanation: Convert the Fahrenheit values: 50 °F = 10 °C and 77 °F = 25 °C. So the order is −10 °C, 0 °C, 10 °C (50 °F), 20 °C, 25 °C (77 °F).

questions.stem: Complete with zu + the verb in brackets, as one word: "Vergiss nicht, den Kunden ___!" (zurückrufen)
questions.explanation: zurückrufen is separable (zurück + rufen), so zu goes between the prefix and the verb and everything is written as one word: zurückzurufen. "zu zurückrufen" puts zu in front as with ordinary verbs.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "I don't have time to print the contract."
questions.explanation: Ich habe keine Zeit, den Vertrag zu drucken. The main clause comes first with the verb in position 2; after the comma, the infinitive clause ends with zu + infinitive, so the object (den Vertrag) comes before "zu drucken".

questions.stem: In which sentences is zu used correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich muss heute länger zu arbeiten.
Es ist wichtig, den Chef anzurufen.
Wir gehen heute Mittag zu essen.
questions.explanation: versuchen and "es ist wichtig" take zu + infinitive, and anrufen puts zu in the middle: anzurufen. müssen is a modal verb, so no zu: Ich muss heute länger arbeiten. gehen + activity takes no zu either: Wir gehen heute Mittag essen.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this office.

image.alt: An office with a chair, a desk with a telephone, a contract on a clipboard and a laptop, and a printer on a cabinet; five parts are numbered

questions.explanation: 1 das Telefon, 2 der Vertrag (the contract with a signature line), 3 der Schreibtisch, 4 der Drucker (printer; drucken = to print), 5 der Stuhl. die Besprechung is a meeting and das Gehalt a salary: neither is an object you can point to.

questions.stem: Match each sentence from a business phone call to its meaning.
left: Er ist gerade in einer Besprechung.
choices: He is in a meeting right now.
questions.explanation: ausrichten = to pass on a message; die Besprechung = meeting; am Apparat = speaking (on the phone); sich krankmelden = to call in sick. "She quit her job" would be: Sie hat gekündigt.

questions.stem: Say "Peter's teacher" in German with the name + s pattern: "___ Lehrerin"
questions.explanation: With a name, German adds -s with no apostrophe and no article: Peters Lehrerin. "Peter's" with an apostrophe is the English spelling; "die Peters Lehrerin" adds an article that this pattern doesn't take.

questions.stem: Which school subject does each numbered picture stand for?

image.alt: Six numbered pictures: a board with sums, a globe, musical notes, a paint palette with a brush, a football and a flask

questions.explanation: 1 Mathe (sums on the board), 2 Erdkunde (geography: the globe), 3 Musik, 4 Kunst (art: palette and brush), 5 Sport, 6 Chemie (the flask). Physik is physics and Geschichte history.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Er ist bei der Prüfung durchgefallen.
Das ist das Auto von mein Bruder.
questions.explanation: bestehen is inseparable (bestanden, no ge-), durchfallen is separable and takes sein (ist durchgefallen), and a name takes -s with no apostrophe (Annas Buch). unterrichten is inseparable, so it's "hat unterrichtet" without ge-, and von takes the dative: von meinem Bruder.

questions.stem: Put the stages of Mia's life in order, as in the text "Mias Weg".
questions.explanation: Mia went to the Grundschule, then to the Gymnasium, which ends with the Abitur. She didn't get a university place, so she did an Ausbildung as a photographer, and today she has her own studio.

questions.stem: Match each German phrase to its English meaning.
choices: at the end of the week
questions.explanation: von meinem Bruder is one brother (dative singular meinem); several brothers would be von meinen Brüdern. "der Woche" and "der Teilnehmer" are genitives (feminine singular and plural). Hans ends in s, so it takes only an apostrophe: Hans' Zeugnis.

questions.stem: Turn the question "Brauche ich einen Termin?" into an indirect question. Complete with one word: "Wissen Sie, ___ ich einen Termin brauche?"
questions.explanation: The direct question "Brauche ich einen Termin?" is a yes/no question, so the indirect question uses ob (whether), and the verb goes to the end. wenn means if/when and can't introduce an indirect question.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order: "Could you tell me how long the repair takes?"
questions.explanation: Könnten Sie mir sagen, wie lange die Reparatur dauert? The question word wie lange starts the indirect question, the subject follows, and the conjugated verb dauert goes to the end. The question mark belongs to the frame "Könnten Sie mir sagen".

questions.stem: In which sentences does someone else do the work? Select all that apply.

image.alt: Left: a woman repairs her own bike, captioned Ich repariere mein Fahrrad. Right: a mechanic repairs her bike, captioned Ich lasse mein Fahrrad reparieren.

choices: Sie lässt sich die Haare schneiden.
questions.explanation: lassen + infinitive means having something done by someone else: the garage repairs the car, the hairdresser cuts her hair. "Ich habe mein Fahrrad repariert" means you did it yourself, and "selbst" says so outright.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: abheben = withdraw, einzahlen = pay in, überweisen = transfer, beantragen = apply for (documents), melden = report. To open an account is "ein Konto eröffnen".

questions.stem: Complete with the present-tense form of lassen: "Er ___ sein Fahrrad reparieren."
questions.explanation: lassen changes its stem in the du and er/sie/es forms: du lässt, er lässt. "lasst" is the ihr form.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of "Tag": "Ich habe seit drei ___ Husten."
questions.explanation: seit takes the dative, and dative plural nouns add -n: seit drei Tagen. "seit drei Tage" forgets the dative -n.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things from the doctor's office.

image.alt: Five numbered things: a sticking plaster, a bandage roll, a syringe, a card with a chip and a photo, and a blister pack of tablets

questions.explanation: 1 das Pflaster (sticking plaster), 2 der Verband (bandage), 3 die Spritze (syringe, injection), 4 die Versichertenkarte (health insurance card), 5 die Tabletten. das Rezept is the prescription, a piece of paper (or an e-prescription), and der Krankenwagen is an ambulance.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a visit to the doctor in order.
choices: In der Praxis anrufen und einen Termin machen
An der Rezeption die Versichertenkarte zeigen
Mit dem Rezept in die Apotheke gehen
questions.explanation: First you call for an appointment, then you show your insurance card at the reception desk when you arrive, the doctor examines you and writes a prescription, and finally you take it to the pharmacy.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct German? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich bin seit einer Woche krank.
Ich habe seit drei Tage Fieber.
Nimm die Tablette nach dem Essen!
Ich habe eine Allergie für Katzen.
questions.explanation: seit + dative + present tense (seit einer Woche), sollte for advice, and the du imperative without -st (Nimm!) are all right. "seit drei Tage" needs the dative plural -n (Tagen), and an allergy is "gegen" something: eine Allergie gegen Katzen.

questions.stem: Match each instruction from a doctor or pharmacist to its meaning.
questions.explanation: täglich = daily, so dreimal täglich is three times a day; alle + time + plural = every (alle vier Stunden); wöchentlich = weekly; nach dem Essen = after meals (before meals is vor dem Essen).

questions.stem: What is "das Anschreiben" in a German job application?
questions.explanation: das Anschreiben is the one-page cover letter. The CV is der Lebenslauf, the reference is das Arbeitszeugnis, and the job advert is die Stellenanzeige.

questions.stem: After an interview, which answer do you hope to get?
questions.explanation: die Zusage is the yes: the job is yours. die Absage is the rejection, die Probezeit the probation period at the start of a job, and die Kündigung the notice when a job ends.

questions.stem: Which CV line says "Ich habe Angebote geschrieben" in the nominal style?
questions.explanation: The nominal style turns the action into a noun (erstellen → die Erstellung) and adds the object with von + dative plural: Erstellung von Angeboten. The other choices still use verb forms.

questions.stem: Turn the verb into a noun for a CV line: "Ich habe die Post bearbeitet." → "___ der Post"
questions.explanation: bearbeiten → die Bearbeitung: verb stem + -ung, a feminine noun. "der Post" is the genitive of die Post, so the line means "dealing with the mail".

questions.stem: Which sentence from an Arbeitszeugnis gives the best grade, in the usual reading?
choices: Sie arbeitete stets zu unserer vollen Zufriedenheit.
Sie arbeitete zu unserer vollen Zufriedenheit.
Sie arbeitete stets zu unserer vollsten Zufriedenheit.
Sie war stets bemüht, gute Arbeit zu leisten.
questions.explanation: stets + vollsten is the top formula (sehr gut). stets + vollen reads as gut, vollen without stets as befriedigend, and "stets bemüht" means she tried without success.

questions.stem: Put these reference formulas in order from the best grade to the worst, using the usual scale from the lesson.
questions.explanation: sehr gut, gut, befriedigend, ausreichend. Each step drops something: first vollsten becomes vollen, then stets goes, then voll goes too. This scale is a widely used convention, not a law.

questions.stem: "Er war stets bemüht, seine Aufgaben zu erledigen." How do HR departments usually read this sentence in a reference?
choices: He tried, but did not succeed.
questions.explanation: It sounds kind ("he always made an effort"), but it says nothing about results, so it's read as a poor grade: he tried and didn't manage. A good reference talks about results and satisfaction, ideally "stets zu unserer vollsten Zufriedenheit".

questions.stem: Lena's CV has its headings hidden. Name the numbered parts.

image.alt: A German CV with a photo and four hidden section headings above personal details, a job, an apprenticeship and school, and languages, with place, date and signature at the bottom; six parts are numbered

questions.explanation: 1 the photo, 2 Persönliche Daten (name, birth date, address), 3 Berufserfahrung (her job since 2019), 4 Ausbildung (apprenticeship and school), 5 Sprachkenntnisse (German and English), 6 place, date and signature. Betreff and Anlagen belong to the cover letter, not the CV.

questions.stem: Which are typical of a German Lebenslauf? Select all that apply.
choices: a table with dates on the left
questions.explanation: A German CV is a table, usually newest first, and explains gaps such as parental leave. Full sentences belong in the cover letter, and salaries don't go on a CV.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a cover letter in order, from top to bottom.
choices: Über eine Einladung … würde ich mich sehr freuen.
questions.explanation: Subject line, greeting, the first line (hiermit bewerbe ich mich …), the closing sentence about an interview, the closing formula, and finally the list of enclosures.

questions.stem: Complete the last line of a cover letter: "Ich freue mich ___, Sie kennenzulernen."
questions.explanation: "Looking forward to" is sich freuen auf; when the thing is an action in a zu-infinitive, auf becomes the da-word darauf: Ich freue mich darauf, Sie kennenzulernen. darüber goes with sich freuen über (being glad about something that has happened).

questions.stem: In Lena's cover letter, why does the new job interest her in particular?
choices: The company is near her flat.
The company works internationally and she wants to improve her English.
questions.explanation: "Ihre Firma arbeitet international, und ich möchte meine Englischkenntnisse im Beruf verbessern. Deshalb interessiert mich diese Stelle besonders." The letter says nothing about salary, distance or part-time work.

questions.stem: Match each word from applications to its meaning.
questions.explanation: hiermit = hereby, sorgfältig = careful, teamfähig = good at teamwork, stets = a formal word for immer, einstellen = to hire. Reliable is zuverlässig; to quit is kündigen.

questions.stem: What does "rezeptfrei" mean?
questions.explanation: rezeptfrei = without a prescription (frei = free of, as in alkoholfrei). It doesn't mean free of charge: you still pay for the medicine.

questions.stem: In Germany, where are most painkillers sold?
choices: only at the doctor's, with a prescription
next to the shampoo in drugstores
questions.explanation: Most painkillers are apothekenpflichtig: you don't need a prescription, but you can only buy them in a pharmacy, where the pharmacist can advise you. Only a few mild remedies are freiverkäuflich.

questions.stem: Match each package-insert heading to what you find in that section.

image.alt: The first page of the package insert for the made-up medicine Musterin 200 mg with its six numbered section headings

left: Was sollten Sie vor der Einnahme beachten?
choices: how much to take and how often
warnings and when not to take it
questions.explanation: Sections 3, 4, 5 and 2 of every EU package insert. einnehmen = to take a medicine, die Nebenwirkung = side effect, aufbewahren = to store, die Einnahme = taking it. Package inserts don't give prices.

questions.stem: A package insert lists a side effect as "gelegentlich". How often does it occur?
questions.explanation: gelegentlich = 1 to 10 in 1,000 people treated. More than 1 in 10 is sehr häufig, 1 to 10 in 100 is häufig, and fewer than 1 in 10,000 is sehr selten.

questions.stem: Put the side-effect words in order from the most frequent to the least frequent.
questions.explanation: sehr häufig (more than 1 in 10), häufig (1–10 in 100), gelegentlich (1–10 in 1,000), selten (1–10 in 10,000), sehr selten (fewer than 1 in 10,000).

questions.stem: The leaflet says: "Erwachsene: 1 Tablette bis zu dreimal täglich. Nehmen Sie nicht mehr als 3 Tabletten pro Tag ein." What is the largest number of tablets an adult may take in 3 days? Give only the number.
questions.explanation: bis zu dreimal täglich, one tablet each time, and never more than 3 a day: 3 × 3 days = 9 tablets at most.

questions.stem: "Die Tabletten werden nach dem Essen eingenommen." What does this mean?
choices: The tablets will be eaten after meals.
The tablets have been taken after meals.
The tablets become effective after meals.
The tablets are taken after meals.
questions.explanation: werden + past participle (eingenommen) is the passive in the present: the tablets are taken. The future would need an infinitive, and "become" needs an adjective or noun after werden.

questions.stem: Which sentences are in the passive? Select all that apply.
choices: Die Salbe wird zweimal täglich aufgetragen.
Ich werde morgen zum Arzt gehen.
Das Mittel wird vom Arzt verschrieben.
questions.explanation: The passive has werden + a past participle: aufgetragen, verschrieben, geraucht. "Ich werde … gehen" has an infinitive (future), and "wird Apotheker" has a noun (to become).

questions.stem: Which article goes with "Schmerzmittel" (painkiller)?
questions.explanation: In a compound noun the last part decides the gender: der Schmerz + das Mittel = das Schmerzmittel. "der" takes the gender from the first part, a common mistake; "den" is accusative.

questions.stem: Make the leaflet sentence active with man: "Die Kapseln werden morgens eingenommen." → "Man ___ die Kapseln morgens ___."
questions.explanation: eingenommen comes from einnehmen, a separable verb with the stem change of nehmen: man nimmt … ein. The prefix ein goes to the end.

questions.stem: A prescription medicine costs 30 euros. How much does an adult with statutory health insurance usually pay at the pharmacy?
questions.explanation: The Zuzahlung is 10 percent of the price, at least 5 and at most 10 euros. 10 percent of 30 euros is 3 euros, which is below the minimum, so you pay 5 euros.

questions.stem: In the pharmacy dialogue, why does the pharmacist ask "Nehmen Sie noch andere Medikamente?"
choices: Because medicines can affect each other.
Because she wants to sell more medicines.
Because Tom has lost his prescription.
Because the cough syrup is sold out.
questions.explanation: Pharmacists ask this because medicines can affect each other. Tom has his prescription, and nothing in the dialogue says the syrup is sold out.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: der Wirkstoff = active ingredient (wirken = to work), die Salbe = ointment, verschreiben = to prescribe, schlucken = to swallow, die Dosierung = dosage. A side effect is die Nebenwirkung, a pharmacist der Apotheker or die Apothekerin.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this official letter.

image.alt: A letter from the Bürgeramt of Musterstadt to Daniel Costa in the standard German layout; six parts are numbered

questions.explanation: 1 the sender (Stadt Musterstadt, Bürgeramt), 2 the address field, 3 the file number in the reference block, 4 the bold subject line, 5 the greeting (Sehr geehrter Herr Costa,), 6 the enclosure. The date is further down in the reference block, and the closing formula (Mit freundlichen Grüßen) comes after the text.

questions.stem: What is a "Mahnung"?
choices: a reminder that a payment is overdue
an official decision on an application
questions.explanation: die Mahnung = payment reminder. An official decision is der Bescheid; a form is das Formular.

questions.stem: "Das Formular ist bis zum 1. April auszufüllen." What does this mean?
choices: The form was filled in by 1 April.
The form must be filled in by 1 April.
The form is closed until 1 April.
questions.explanation: sein + zu + infinitive (ist … auszufüllen) means something must be done. The zu belongs to the infinitive (ausfüllen → auszufüllen), not "too" or "closed".

questions.stem: Complete the official sentence with zu + infinitive, as one word: "Die Unterlagen sind dem Antrag ___." (beifügen)
questions.explanation: beifügen is separable (bei + fügen), so zu goes in the middle: beizufügen. The sentence means "The documents must be enclosed with the application."

questions.stem: Match each abbreviation to its full form.
questions.explanation: z. B. = for example, bzw. = or rather / respectively, ggf. = if necessary, i. A. = on behalf of, u. a. = among other things. und so weiter is usw., and das heißt is d. h.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "The amount must be paid by 15 March."
questions.explanation: Der Betrag ist bis zum 15. März zu zahlen. sein is the verb in position 2, the time phrase sits in the middle, and zu + infinitive closes the sentence.

questions.stem: Look back at the reminder in Example 3. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
choices: The money must be transferred by 15 February 2026.
The letter is about fees for collecting rubbish.
Nothing happens if you don't pay.
questions.explanation: 96 euros of Müllgebühren + a 5-euro Mahngebühr = 101 euros, to be transferred (ist … zu überweisen) by 15 February. The reminder fee is 5 euros, not 96, and "Bei Nichtzahlung müssen wir weitere Schritte einleiten" warns of further steps.

questions.stem: What does "nach Eingang Ihrer Zahlung" mean?
choices: after you have entered the building
questions.explanation: der Eingang comes from eingehen (to arrive, be received), and Ihrer Zahlung is a genitive: "after the arrival of your payment", in everyday German "wenn Ihre Zahlung angekommen ist". Eingang can mean entrance, but not in this phrase.

questions.stem: You disagree with a Bescheid from the Finanzamt. Where in the letter do you find how and by when you can object?
questions.explanation: The Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung at the end of every Bescheid says how to challenge it. For a decision from the Finanzamt that is an Einspruch, usually within one month (for most other authorities it's a Widerspruch). The Betreff names the topic, the Anrede is the greeting, and the Aktenzeichen is the file number.

questions.stem: "Sie haben die Unterlagen bis Freitag vorzulegen." What does this mean?
choices: You have presented the documents by Friday.
You must present the documents by Friday.
You have no documents until Friday.
You may present the documents after Friday.
questions.explanation: haben + zu + infinitive = müssen, in a strict tone. It isn't the perfect tense, which would need a past participle (vorgelegt).

questions.stem: What does "i. A. Brenner" before a signature mean?
choices: Ms Brenner signs on behalf of her office.
Ms Brenner is the person the letter is sent to.
questions.explanation: i. A. = im Auftrag, on behalf of. The person signs for the office or company, not personally. Enclosures are listed under Anlage(n).

questions.stem: In the letter from the Bürgeramt, what must Daniel hand in by 26 February?
choices: a copy of his rental contract
questions.explanation: "bei Ihrer Anmeldung … fehlte die Wohnungsgeberbestätigung. Bitte reichen Sie diese bis zum 26.02.2026 … ein." The rental contract appears in Example 2 and the 101 euros in the reminder of Example 3, not in this letter.

questions.stem: Write out the abbreviation "usw." in full.
questions.explanation: usw. = und so weiter (and so on, etc.). Like z. B. (zum Beispiel), it's read aloud in full.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this laptop and web page.

image.alt: A laptop with a web page on the screen: a password box at the top right, a video player, an advert saying -50 % Jetzt kaufen!, and a comment saying Tolles Video, danke! Six numbered markers.

questions.explanation: 1 is the screen (der Bildschirm), 2 the keyboard (die Tastatur), 3 the video (das Video), 4 the advert (die Werbung: "-50 %, Jetzt kaufen!"), 5 a comment under the video (der Kommentar) and 6 the password box (das Passwort). A printer (der Drucker) isn't in the picture, and die Sendung is a TV or radio programme.

questions.stem: Type the relative pronoun: "Das ist das Video, ___ ich gestern hochgeladen habe."
questions.explanation: Video is neuter (das Video), and inside the relative clause "ich" is the subject: I uploaded the video, so it is the object. Neuter accusative = das. Only the masculine changes in the accusative (den).

questions.stem: Type the relative pronoun (dative plural): "Das sind die Nachbarn, ___ ich unser WLAN-Passwort gegeben habe."
questions.explanation: I gave the password to the neighbours: they are the dative object of geben, and Nachbarn is plural. The dative plural relative pronoun is denen, with an extra -en (the article would be den).

questions.stem: Put the words in order to make a correct sentence: "The laptop I bought was expensive."
questions.explanation: "Der Laptop, den ich gekauft habe, war teuer." The relative clause comes straight after its noun, starts with the relative pronoun (den: masculine, object) and ends with the conjugated verb (habe). Then the main clause goes on with its verb: "habe, war" is the verb-comma-verb pattern.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich habe eine App, die sehr gut ist.
Das ist der Film, den ich gesehen habe.
Das ist die Frau, der das Video gemacht hat.
Kennst du das Programm, das ich habe heruntergeladen?
questions.explanation: "eine App, die sehr gut ist" (feminine, subject) and "der Film, den ich gesehen habe" (masculine, object) are right. In the third sentence the woman made the video, so she is the subject: "die Frau, die das Video gemacht hat". In the fourth, the verb must go to the end: "das ich heruntergeladen habe".

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the relative pronoun that fills the gap.
questions.explanation: Gender and number come from the noun, case from the job inside the clause. I know the colleague: masculine accusative, den. Everyone uses the app: feminine accusative, die. The phone is broken: neuter nominative, das. mit takes the dative, plural: denen. helfen takes the dative, masculine: dem.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this room in December.

image.alt: A living room in December: a decorated Christmas tree with a star on top, an Advent calendar with numbered doors on the wall, a present under the tree and a candle on a table by a window. Five numbered markers.

questions.explanation: 1 is the star on top of the tree (der Stern), 2 the Christmas tree (der Weihnachtsbaum), 3 the Advent calendar with its numbered doors (der Adventskalender), 4 a present (das Geschenk) and 5 a candle (die Kerze). Fireworks (das Feuerwerk) belong to Silvester, and a Torte is a cream cake; neither is in the picture.

questions.stem: Put these days in the order they come in the festive year, starting with Advent.
questions.explanation: The first Sunday of Advent is the fourth Sunday before Christmas (between 27 November and 3 December); Heiligabend is 24 December, Silvester 31 December, Neujahr 1 January. The Karneval season officially opens on 11 November, but the street carnival (Rosenmontag, Fasching parades) comes in February or March, just before Lent, so it always comes before Easter (Ostern).

questions.stem: Write the ordinal in words: "Am 24. Dezember feiern wir." is read "Am ___ Dezember feiern wir."
questions.explanation: From 20 on, ordinals add -ste: vierundzwanzigste. After am (an dem) the ordinal takes -en: am vierundzwanzigsten Dezember.

questions.stem: Answer with one word: "Hast du eine Kerze für mich?" – "Ja, hier ist ___."
questions.explanation: Kerze is feminine, so the pronoun is eine, just like the article. Only the masculine nominative (einer) and the neuter (eins) differ from the article.

questions.stem: It is the afternoon of 31 December. Which wishes fit? Select all that apply.
choices: Einen guten Rutsch ins neue Jahr!
questions.explanation: Before midnight on Silvester, people say "Guten Rutsch!" or the longer "Einen guten Rutsch ins neue Jahr!". "Frohe Ostern" is for Easter, and "Frohe Weihnachten" is too late on 31 December.

questions.stem: Match each beginning to the word that fills the gap: wann, wenn or als.
left: ___ ich klein war, waren wir an Silvester bei Oma.
___ es schneit, gehen wir mit Fackeln in den Wald.
___ du kommst, backe ich eine Torte.
questions.explanation: als is for one period or event in the past (when I was little). wenn is for things that happen again and again (whenever it snows) and for the present and future (when you come). wann asks a question, also inside an indirect question (Weißt du, wann …?).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this e-mail.

image.alt: An e-mail in a mail program: the An line with an address, the Betreff line Termin am 12. Juni, an attachment called heizung.jpg, the opening Sehr geehrter Herr Wagner, the text, the closing Mit freundlichen Grüßen and the name Anna Lindqvist. Five numbered markers.

questions.explanation: 1 is the recipient in the An line (der Empfänger), 2 the subject line (der Betreff), 3 the attachment (der Anhang), 4 the opening (die Anrede: Sehr geehrter Herr Wagner,) and 5 the closing (der Gruß: Mit freundlichen Grüßen). The sender (der Absender) and a signature (die Unterschrift) are not marked.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this formal e-mail in order.
choices: leider bin ich an diesem Tag nicht zu Hause.
questions.explanation: Subject line first, then the opening with a comma, then the text starting with a small letter (leider), the problem before the request, then the closing without a comma and the name on its own line.

questions.stem: Complete the closing of a formal e-mail: "Mit freundlichen ___"
questions.explanation: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen" is the standard formal closing. Grüßen is dative plural after mit (der Gruß, die Grüße, mit den Grüßen). In Switzerland it is spelled Grüssen.

questions.stem: You write a semi-formal e-mail to your course teacher, Anna Brandt. Which openings are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Semi-formal openings use Frau or Herr with the surname: "Liebe Frau Brandt," or "Hallo Frau Brandt,". "Lieber" is for a man (Lieber Herr Yilmaz), and Frau never goes with a first name.

questions.stem: Match each message to its register.
left: An e-mail to the landlord you know and call Sie
A letter to an office you have never contacted
A chat message to a classmate
A request to a company you don't know
questions.explanation: Family, friends and classmates you call du get informal messages. People you know but call Sie (a teacher, a neighbour, a landlord) get semi-formal ones: Liebe Frau …, Viele Grüße. Offices, companies and strangers get formal ones: Sehr geehrte …, Mit freundlichen Grüßen.

questions.stem: To pass the Goethe-Zertifikat A2 you need at least ___ of the 100 points. Give only the number.
questions.explanation: 60 of 100 points overall, and also at least 45 of the 75 written points and 15 of the 25 speaking points.

questions.stem: Which of these results pass the Goethe-Zertifikat A2? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: All three conditions must hold: at least 45 written, at least 15 speaking, at least 60 in all. 50 + 15 = 65 and 46 + 20 = 66 pass. 72 in all fails because 12 speaking points are under 15; 69 in all fails because 44 written points are under 45.

questions.stem: Match each part of the Goethe A2 to one of its tasks.
choices: An SMS and a semi-formal e-mail
Planning an appointment with a partner
A prepared presentation on your own
questions.explanation: Lesen includes matching people to ads; Hören includes announcements and phone messages; Schreiben has an informal SMS and a semi-formal e-mail; Sprechen ends with planning something together with your partner. There is no prepared solo presentation at A2.

questions.stem: Put this planning conversation in order.
choices: Am Samstag kann ich leider nicht. Geht es am Sonntag?
Ja, Sonntag passt mir. Um wie viel Uhr?
Wie wäre es mit zehn Uhr?
questions.explanation: Suggest a day, react (refuse with a new suggestion), accept the day and ask for a time, suggest a time, agree. This suggest–react–agree pattern is exactly what the planning task wants.

questions.stem: A result of 60 to 69 points has the grade ___ (one German word).
questions.explanation: 60–69 is ausreichend (sufficient, a pass); 70–79 befriedigend, 80–89 gut, 90–100 sehr gut.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this newspaper page.

image.alt: The front page of an invented local paper, the Neckar-Bote: a large two-line headline, two bold sentences under it, a photo of a bridge with a line of small italic text under it, and columns of text. Five numbered markers.

questions.explanation: 1 is the headline (die Schlagzeile), 2 the bold lead under it (der Vorspann), 3 the photo, 4 the caption under the photo (die Bildunterschrift) and 5 the body of the article (der Text). There is no advert or comment on this page.

questions.stem: What does the headline "Streik bei der Bahn: Tausende Pendler warten" say?
choices: The railway is on strike, and thousands of commuters are waiting.
The railway wants to stop a strike by thousands of commuters.
Thousands of commuters are going on strike against the railway.
The railway is waiting for thousands of new commuters.
questions.explanation: The topic before the colon is a strike at the railway (der Streik, from streiken); the news after it is that thousands of commuters are waiting. Headlines leave out articles and verbs like sein, so rebuild the sentence: Die Bahn streikt, deshalb warten Tausende Pendler.

questions.stem: A headline says: "Feuerwehr rettet Katze vom Dach". When did the rescue happen?
choices: It is happening right now, live.
questions.explanation: Headlines use the present tense for events that already happened. The report under it will tell the story in the simple past: Die Feuerwehr rettete gestern eine Katze.

questions.stem: What does "laut" mean in "Laut Polizei war der Fahrer zu schnell"?
questions.explanation: The preposition laut means "according to" and names the source: according to the police, the driver was going too fast. It has nothing to do with the adjective laut (loud).

questions.stem: What does "Das neue Museum soll 30 Millionen Euro kosten" mean?
choices: The new museum should cost 30 million euros.
The new museum is said to cost 30 million euros.
The new museum must not cost more than 30 million euros.
The new museum cost 30 million euros.
questions.explanation: In news, sollen usually passes on what others say: "is said to, reportedly". The writer doesn't promise that the figure is right. "should cost" is the tempting word-for-word translation, but the sentence isn't advice or a plan.

questions.stem: Type the simple past of geben: "Gestern ___ es einen Unfall auf der A8."
questions.explanation: geben is a strong verb: gab in the simple past (es gab = there was / there were). News reports use the simple past; in speech you would say "Gestern hat es einen Unfall gegeben."

questions.stem: Type the relative pronoun: "Das ist die Firma, bei ___ mein Bruder arbeitet."
questions.explanation: bei always takes the dative, and Firma is feminine, so: bei der. The preposition comes first, then the relative pronoun, and the verb goes to the end (arbeitet).

questions.stem: Complete: "Das ist die Brücke, über ___ täglich 8.000 Autos fahren."
questions.explanation: Brücke is feminine, and über here takes the accusative because the cars move across the bridge. Feminine accusative: die. "der" would be the dative, used for a position: über der Brücke means above the bridge.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "That is the man the police spoke with."
questions.explanation: "Das ist der Mann, mit dem die Polizei gesprochen hat." The preposition comes first in the relative clause, never at the end as in English. mit + dative masculine = dem, and the auxiliary hat comes last, after the participle.

questions.stem: Headlines use nouns made from verbs. Match each noun to its verb.
questions.explanation: Many news nouns come from verbs: -ung nouns (die Eröffnung, die Verletzung) are feminine; der Streik and die Wahl drop the ending. erscheinen (to come out) matches none of them.

questions.stem: Which sentences tell you that a fact is not confirmed? Select all that apply.
choices: Der Täter soll etwa 30 Jahre alt sein.
Angeblich war der Fahrer sehr müde.
questions.explanation: Hearsay soll (is said to be) and angeblich (allegedly) both pass on unconfirmed information. The other two state facts directly: the bridge was built in 1950 (a passive), the fire began at about 5.

questions.stem: Read: "Das Feuer begann laut Feuerwehr gegen 5 Uhr in der Backstube, wo zu dieser Zeit schon zwei Mitarbeiter arbeiteten. Eine Nachbarin, die den Rauch sah, rief sofort die Feuerwehr." Who called the fire brigade?
questions.explanation: "Eine Nachbarin, die den Rauch sah, rief sofort die Feuerwehr": a neighbour who saw the smoke called at once. The employees were in the bakehouse, where (wo) the fire began.

questions.stem: Which way of reporting a quote is correct?
choices: „Wir sind froh“, sagte sie die Besitzerin.
questions.explanation: The quote fills position 1, so the verb comes next and then the speaker: „…“, sagte die Besitzerin. The first choice keeps English order; the third repeats the subject; the fourth puts the verb at the end as in a subordinate clause.

questions.stem: Which phrase means the same as "die Stadt, wo der Unfall passierte"?
choices: die Stadt, in die der Unfall passierte
die Stadt, der der Unfall passierte
die Stadt, in der der Unfall passierte
die Stadt, wohin der Unfall passierte
questions.explanation: For a place (where?), wo = in + dative: die Stadt, in der … (feminine dative). "in die" and "wohin" would mean movement into the town; "der" without a preposition means "to which".

questions.stem: A website promises "aktuelle Nachrichten". What does it offer?
questions.explanation: aktuell means current, up to date. It is a false friend: "actual" in the sense of real is tatsächlich.

questions.stem: You only have time to read part of an article but want who, what, when and where. What do you read?
choices: the last paragraph with the quotes
the name of the newspaper and the date
questions.explanation: News reports put the most important facts first: the headline gives the news in a few words and the lead answers the main W-questions. Background and quotes come last, so they are what an editor cuts first.

questions.stem: On their first day of school, what do children in Germany usually carry?
choices: a Schultüte, a big cone of sweets and school things
questions.explanation: At the Einschulung every new pupil carries a Schultüte (Zuckertüte in parts of the east), filled with sweets, small toys and things like pens. Old plates belong to the Polterabend.

questions.stem: Your German friend's birthday is tomorrow, and you see her today. What do most Germans expect?
choices: You congratulate her today, to be the first.
You don't congratulate her yet; you wait until the day.
questions.explanation: Congratulating before the birthday is widely thought to bring bad luck, so wait for the day. Afterwards you can still say "Alles Gute nachträglich!". Herzliches Beileid is said when someone has died.

questions.stem: In Germany, Austria and Switzerland, where does a couple become legally married?
questions.explanation: Only the civil ceremony (die Trauung) at the Standesamt, the registry office, makes a marriage legal. A church wedding is optional and usually comes after it.

questions.stem: What do guests traditionally do at a Polterabend?
choices: They smash old china, and the couple sweep it up together.
They smash glasses and mirrors for luck.
They sweep the steps of the cathedral.
They bring bread and salt for the new flat.
questions.explanation: Guests break old plates and cups (Scherben bringen Glück), and the couple sweep up together. Glass and mirrors are traditionally avoided. Sweeping cathedral steps is a Bremen custom for unmarried 30-year-olds, and bread and salt is a housewarming present.

questions.stem: Complete the birthday wish with one word: "___ Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!"
questions.explanation: "Herzlichen Glückwunsch!" The wish is the object of an understood sentence (I give you my warm congratulations), so it is accusative; Glückwunsch is masculine and there is no article, so the adjective takes -en. "Herzlicher" would be nominative.

questions.stem: "Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum 40. Geburtstag!" Write the ordinal in words: "zum ___ Geburtstag".
questions.explanation: 40 → vierzig + -ste (from 20 on), and after zum (zu dem) the ending is -en: zum vierzigsten Geburtstag.

questions.stem: Match each wish to the situation it fits.
choices: The last days before New Year
questions.explanation: Guten Rutsch is said before 1 January, Gute Besserung to someone who is ill, Herzliches Beileid after a death, and Viel Erfolg (good luck, lots of success) before an exam or a new job. For a wedding you would say Herzlichen Glückwunsch zur Hochzeit.

questions.stem: Put this condolence card in order.
choices: es tut uns sehr leid, dass Ihr Vater gestorben ist.
Wir sind in Gedanken bei Ihnen und Ihrer Familie.
questions.explanation: Opening with a comma, then the text starting with a small letter (es tut uns leid …), then the thought for the family, the closing In stiller Anteilnahme and the names.

questions.stem: Which wishes are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Wishes are accusative with strong endings: masculine Glückwunsch → herzlichen, neuter Wochenende → schönes. "Herzlicher" is the nominative ending, and Geburtstag is masculine, so "Frohe Geburtstag" is wrong; say "Alles Gute zum Geburtstag!".

questions.stem: Why does "Guten Rutsch!" end in -en?
choices: Because the wish is the object of an understood "Ich wünsche dir …", and der Rutsch is masculine.
Because all wishes are in the dative.
questions.explanation: Wishes are ellipses: "(Ich wünsche dir einen) guten Rutsch". The wish is the direct object, so accusative; der Rutsch is masculine, and with no article the adjective takes -en.

questions.stem: Your grandparents celebrate their Silberhochzeit. How long have they been married?
questions.explanation: The Silberhochzeit (silver wedding) is after 25 years; the Goldene Hochzeit (golden wedding) after 50.

questions.stem: Read: "Wir haben alles auf den Boden geworfen, und am Ende mussten Julia und Max die Scherben zusammen wegfegen. Das hat zwei Stunden gedauert!" What did Julia and Max do?
choices: They threw the plates on the ground.
They swept up the broken pieces together.
They bought new plates for two hours.
They went home after two hours.
questions.explanation: "mussten … die Scherben zusammen wegfegen": they had to sweep away the broken pieces together, which took two hours. The guests (wir) threw the plates.

questions.stem: Complete the opening of a card to a couple: "Liebe Lena, ___ Tom,"
questions.explanation: Each name gets its own form: liebe for a woman, lieber for a man. After the comma it is written with a small letter, so "lieber", not "Lieber".

questions.stem: Friends invite you to their Einweihungsparty. What is a traditional present?
questions.explanation: An Einweihungsparty is a housewarming, and bread and salt (Brot und Salz) is the traditional present, so the household never lacks the basics. Black-bordered cards are for condolences, Schultüten for the first school day, old plates for the Polterabend.

questions.stem: What is a Junggesellenabschied?
choices: a party for a child's first school day
a stag or hen party before a wedding
questions.explanation: A Junggesellenabschied (JGA) is the party friends give the bride or groom before the wedding, often in costumes through town. A Junggeselle is a bachelor; Abschied means farewell.

cards.back: Reading very fast for the topic, the text type and who it is for. Headline, first sentences, big print; don't stop at unknown words.
Hunting for one fact by its shape: Uhr or a colon for a time, Euro or € for a price, a month or a dot for a date. Then read only that line.
Reading one part slowly and completely, small words included. Use it for rules, conditions and instructions.

cards.front: The efficient order for a reading task
cards.back: Read the question → skim the text → scan for the right place → read that part in detail.
erst = not until, later than expected (erst um 10: not before 10). nur = only, limits an amount (nur zwei Tickets).
except: täglich außer montags = every day except Mondays (closed on Mondays).
ab = from … onwards (17-year-olds can't). bis spätestens = by … at the latest (Saturday is too late).
Aushang: a notice from someone in charge (An alle Mieter …). Anzeige: a small ad that offers or wants something (Zu verkaufen, Suche …).
entlaufen or vermisst, a description of the animal, Belohnung (reward), where to ring or call.

cards.front: The lead of a news report
cards.back: The first sentence or paragraph: Wer? Was? Wann? Wo? Quotes, details and Warum? come later.
A plan, not a fact: sollen and bald point to the future. Don't answer as if it has already happened.
From the back: the head word says what it is; the modifier says what kind. der Hausschuh = a shoe for the house (slipper).

cards.front: Gender and plural of a compound
cards.back: Both come from the head word: das Haus + die Tür = die Haustür, plural die Haustüren.
-s-, -n-/-en-, -e- (Wohnungsschlüssel, Sonnenbrille, Hundeleine) carry no meaning. After -ung, -heit, -keit: -s-.
The verb drops its infinitive ending (sometimes keeping -e-): schreiben + Tisch = der Schreibtisch; warten + Zimmer = das Wartezimmer.
-bar: can be done (essbar). -los: without (arbeitslos, kostenlos). un-: the opposite (unbekannt).
-er: person or machine (der Fahrer, der Drucker). -ung: action or result (die Lösung). -heit/-keit: a quality (die Sicherheit, die Sauberkeit).
das Gift = poison; bekommen = to get; also = so, therefore; der Chef = the boss.
aktuell = current; eventuell = possibly; sensibel = sensitive; das Handy = mobile phone.
creepy, eerie; in speech also "incredibly" (unheimlich nett). A reminder to check every guess from word parts.

cards.front: Before you look a word up
cards.back: Verb → infinitive (kauft … ein → einkaufen; fand → finden). Noun → singular (Bäume → der Baum). Adjective → no ending (neuen → neu).
hab (habe), ham (haben), is (ist), nich/net (nicht), 'n/'ne/'nen (ein/eine/einen), mal (einmal), grad (gerade), vorm (vor dem), fürs (für das).
ja, doch, mal, halt, eben, denn: they add attitude, not facts. Komm doch mit! Kannst du mal helfen? Das ist halt so.
ne? (north), gell?/gelt? (south, Austria), oder? (everywhere, especially Switzerland), nicht wahr? (careful speech).
also, na ja, ähm, tja, sozusagen: time to think, no information.
The last version counts: um sieben, nee, warte, um halb acht → 7:30. Listen for nee, warte, Moment, sondern.

cards.front: The shape of a station announcement
cards.back: Attention (Achtung an Gleis 7) → train (number, destination, time) → what's different → what to do / apology.

cards.front: fällt aus / hat Verspätung / heute von Gleis 2
cards.back: is cancelled / is delayed / leaves from platform 2 today.
Units before tens: vierundsechzig = 64; write the 4, then put the 6 in front. siebzehn 17 vs siebzig 70.
2:30, half way to three. Not 3:30.
Only nouns, numbers, times, places. Prepare wer? was? wann? wo? before you listen.
The narrator uses the simple past (Sie nahm den Vogel); characters speak in the present and perfect (Du hast mir geholfen).
Es war einmal … / Und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind, dann leben sie noch heute.
eines Tages (one day), plötzlich (suddenly), da (then), zum Glück (luckily), am Ende (in the end).
Kinder- und Hausmärchen by Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm; the first volume appeared in 1812.
hieß (heißen), trug (tragen), flog (fliegen), sang (singen), grub (graben), half (helfen).
